rows.10:95e4:
Huh? Nakayama, you ask?
She comes to school as if nothing happened.
Morikawa says Nakayama did it, but the police don't seem to believe him.
This is what I heard when I went to visit Morikawa in the hospital.
He didn't seem to me to be lying.{p}
rows.10:9f64:
...Shall we get back to Morikawa?
Seeing someone die made him truly feel what life meant for the first time.
I suppose he realized that the life of a living thing isn't something to be treated lightly.
But by then it was too late.
For a while, Morikawa lived tormented by regret and self-reproach.
He changed a great deal, you know.
Of course he stopped killing animals, and what's more, he often scolded people who left food on their plates, saying no living thing's life should be taken for nothing.{p}
rows.10:a2c0:
...After Morikawa's death, something that seemed to be a suicide note was found in his room, but all it did was flatly set down the facts about the hamster.
Why would he leave something like that, I wonder?
Was he thinking about his own sin as he wrote it?
Or was he thinking about Nakayama's death?
Or perhaps he wanted to say that human lives are just as fleeting as the lives of the animals he had so easily killed...
Why did Morikawa kill himself, when he had realized how precious life is?
Can anyone say that his regret and suffering weighed more than that life?{p}
rows.10:a6fc:
The going-home music played, and silence fell over the school.
For a while, he had time to kill.{p}
rows.10:c584:
The sound of his own footsteps climbing the stairs one by one echoed through the silent space.
Somehow, a solemn feeling had come over him.{p}
rows.10:dfb8:
Aizawa was beaten like a punching bag.
Battered and bruised, Aizawa screamed,
"I'm sorry, but I just had to know.
If a person falls off a roof, do they die, or what happens?"
That was the reason he gave, I'm told.
And then Kuwahata,{p}
rows.10:e3fc:
Aizawa said this, and the two of them hurried down the stairs to see whether the teacher was dead or alive.
It was after school and the place was deserted, so luckily no crowd gathered.{p}
rows.10:eaa4:
Then he saw Kuwahata's and the teacher's faces floating in midair.
They looked happy, and they were saying this:
"How wonderful."
"Magnificent."
"Come on, Aizawa, you too."
"It's all thanks to you, Aizawa.
Who knew it'd be such a great place?"
"Kuwahata, by rights someone like you shouldn't be able to come here."
"Aw, don't say that."
Aizawa had always been interested in jumping.
He couldn't hold himself back any longer.
"Kuwahata... Sir..."
He climbed over the railing and jumped.{p}
rows.10:fda4:
The next day, the school was in an uproar.
Not because Aizawa's body had been found.
But because, on top of the two who had already gone missing, two more had gone missing.
In other words, Aizawa's body had gone off somewhere too.
The police began searching for the four of them, but nothing definite turned up.
There were reports that the four had been seen shuffling along a road on the day Aizawa went missing, but...
It was decided that they had run away from home.
In the end, the only ones who know the truth are all of you and me.{p}
rows.10:10acc:
So this time, Aizawa decided to try strangling his prey.
He tightened his grip carefully, so as not to kill him.
And then the friend went limp.
Aizawa tried to stuff his guinea pig into the burlap sack he'd prepared in advance.
That was when he realized the friend was dead.{p}
